structures.label: common and internal carotid artery (right; mirrored from the left)

description: In the midline the trachea lies a centimetre or two below the skin above the suprasternal notch, with the thyroid isthmus over its upper rings and the great vessels behind the manubrium below. Either side, under the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid, the common carotid artery (pulsating) and lateral to it the internal jugular vein lie in the carotid sheath. Above the medial clavicle the dome of the pleura rises into the root of the neck.

review.notes: Depths below the skin of the lungs, organs, bones and great vessels are measured on one reference body (a 38-year-old man of about 90 kg) and scaled to each patient by height and BMI; the rest is schematic. Not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.

provenance.notes: Depth grid (1.5 cm): depths of the trachea, larynx, cervical vertebrae, lung apices and great vessels measured by rays on the reference body; the left common carotid artery is measured and the right mirrored from it; the jugular veins, thyroid lobes and the borders of sternocleidomastoid are schematic.
